module.title: Module settings
module.description:
Settings of the 879-9000 module, read from it just now. Saving writes the changes to the module, stores them there and makes the module use them. The serial side stays fixed to the meter: {modbus_port}, {baud_rate} baud, parity {parity}.

A new address or DHCP moves the module away from its old address. With a fixed address the entry follows it; with DHCP the search finds it again as long as it is in one of Home Assistant's subnets.

data_description.dhcp: Take the address from a DHCP server instead of the fixed one below.
data_description.ip_address: Fixed address of the module. Kept for when DHCP is off.
data_description.netmask: Netmask of the fixed address, for example 255.255.255.0.
data_description.gateway: Router for other networks; empty for none. Has to be in the module's network.
data_description.ntp: Set the module's clock from a time server.
data_description.ntp_server_1: Address of a time server; empty for none.
data_description.ntp_server_2: Address of a second time server; empty for none.
data_description.hostname: Name the module gives a DHCP server: letters, digits and hyphens.
data_description.timeout: How long the module waits for the meter's answer.

error.invalid_address: Enter an IPv4 address such as 192.168.1.10
error.invalid_hostname: A host name has letters, digits and hyphens only, and neither starts nor ends with a hyphen
error.gateway_outside_network: The gateway has to be another address in the module's network
error.module_write_failed: The module did not accept the settings. If its address changed, the entry follows it once the search finds the module.

abort.module_not_answering: The module did not answer; its settings cannot be shown
abort.module_not_applied: The module stored the settings but did not confirm using them. It uses them after its next restart at the latest.

yaml_still_active.title: The YAML modbus block still serves this meter
yaml_still_active.description:
{entity_id} is still served by the YAML `modbus:` configuration, so its history cannot move to this integration yet.

Remove the `modbus:` block for this meter from your configuration and restart Home Assistant. The integration then takes the entity ids over by itself.

unique_id_taken.title: A meter entity is in the way of the migration
unique_id_taken.description:
{entity_id} cannot move to {unique_id}: that unique id is already registered as {held_by}.

Remove {held_by} under Settings -> Entities. The integration retries on its own.

removed_entry_in_the_way.title: A deleted entity is in the way of the migration
removed_entry_in_the_way.description:
{entity_id} cannot be kept: Home Assistant still remembers a deleted entity for {unique_id} and would bring it back as {restored} instead.

Home Assistant forgets deleted entities 30 days after their removal and offers no way to do it sooner. Either wait until then, or stop Home Assistant, back up, and remove the entry with the entity id {restored} from `deleted_entities` in `.storage/core.entity_registry`. The integration retries on its own.

entity_id_taken.title: An entity id could not be kept
entity_id_taken.description:
{entity_id} could not be kept: the registry gave {created}.

Remove the stale entity holding {entity_id}, then reload the integration.
